parsed.attack: Google discontinued Glass Enterprise Edition 2 on 15 March 2023 with support ending that September, and that was the strongest possible version of this use case: hands-busy workers documenting physical work, with corporate budgets paying for the hardware, a working capture stack, and a decade of Google behind it. It did not die of a closed developer platform or of inference cost - both of which the unlock addresses - it died because not enough people doing hands-busy work would wear a display to record it. Vreal [45] supplies the second cause, "ahead of their time in a market not fully developed" with an installed base that never reached the size the model required, and here the model needs 500 sales at $30 with zero ad spend from the intersection of people who own a first-generation Ray-Ban Display and are mid-teardown on a project bike.
parsed.strongest_defence: The Ray-Ban Display is bought for other reasons, so unlike Glass EE2 this product never has to justify the hardware - it only has to be the best thing to do with a device already on someone's face, and a $30 one-time price needs no enterprise procurement.
parsed.verdict_reason: Glass Enterprise Edition 2 died in 2023 doing precisely this job for a better-funded audience, and Vreal's installed-base cause is more acute for a hobbyist slice of a first-generation display's owners than it was for VR.
